title: Bohol International Marathon 2027 Review: What the 2026 Race Was Like
seo_title: Bohol International Marathon Review: Field, Aid, Times
meta_description: Bohol International Marathon 2026 review: 5,600+ runners on Panglao, DJs and a sari-sari store stop on the course, winning and podium times, and what was never published.
dek: What is known about the 2026 race on Panglao on 30 August: the size of the field, the support on the course, how fast the podiums were, and what the organisers never published.
verdict: Enter if you want a destination race on Panglao with a podium within reach. The 2026 race drew more than 5,600 runners, up from 3,000 in 2024, and the organisers put their effort into the travelling runner: welcome lounges at the airport and seaport, DJs and enhanced hydration stations on the course, and a sari-sari store stop with local snacks. Third place in the women's marathon was 3:39:47. The catch is how little is published: no start times, route map or time limits for 2026 could be found, and there is no airport weather record for race morning. Ask the organiser for all three before you book, and reserve a room early.

sections.heading: The 2026 Race: A Record Field on Panglao
paragraphs: The 2026 BE Grand Bohol International Marathon, subtitled The Sandugo Run, was held on Sunday 30 August [1]. Cebu Daily News reported a record field of more than 5,600 local and international runners, who took to the roads of Panglao at dawn, and a race weekend that filled hotels, restaurants and resorts across the island [2]. The 2024 race had 3,000 participants [3].

The report calls 2026 the fourth edition and describes the race as World Athletics-accredited [2]. BE Grand Resort Bohol signed a three-year hosting deal in 2024, after the previous year's race, and the race was renamed after it [4]; on race day in 2026 the partnership was extended through 2030 [2].

sections.heading: On the Course: DJs, Hydration and a Sari-Sari Store
paragraphs: The organisers' focus in 2026 was looking after visiting runners. There were welcome lounges at the airport and seaport and carbo-loading at the start line, and on the course there were mobile DJs, enhanced hydration stations and, for the first time, a sari-sari store stop offering local snacks [2]. Organiser Michael Yu said the teams were ready to support runners from the airport to the finish line [2]. Local food on the route is not new: the 2024 race had stations serving lechon baka and lechon baboy [3].
There is no airport weather record for race morning: the public archive of airport observations holds nothing for the Bohol-Panglao airport on 30 August 2026 [5].

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: The report lists the top three in each race without naming the distances; judging by the times, they are the marathon, half marathon, 10 km and 5 km [2]. On that reading, Glady Kiptoo won the marathon in 2:32:40 from Edsel Moral (2:37:38) and Florendo Lapiz (2:45:34), and Abigael Jerop won the women's race in 3:21:40 from April Joy Alampayan (3:36:30) and Lucita Fernandez (3:39:47) [2].

The half marathon went to Jhonn Marc Dizon in 1:14:32 and Mary Rose Frias in 1:40:33; third woman ran 1:53:18. The 10 km was won in 32:25 and 41:58, and the 5 km in 15:46 and 20:29 [2]. The pace at the front has risen: the 2024 marathon was won in 2:41:31 and 3:55:28 [3]. A woman who can run under 3:40 had a podium place in 2026, but most runners will not be racing for position. The organiser posted full results after the race [6].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2027 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a marathon holiday on Panglao, a growing field and on-course support with local flavour. It is also a realistic podium chance for a woman around 3:40 or a man around 2:45.

Think twice if you need to know the start time, the route and the time limit before you enter. None of them for 2026 could be found in any published source, and nor could the 2026 entry fees. For reference, in 2025 the marathon cost ₱3,100, the half ₱2,800 and the 10 km and 5 km ₱1,700 each; the 42 km, 21 km and 10 km included an event shirt, a medal, a finisher shirt and a post-race meal, and race kits were collected at the BE Grand Convention Center over the two days before the race [7].

The resort's hosting deal runs through 2030 [2], and the 2027 race is on Sunday 22 August 2027, according to its entry page. Book a room as soon as you enter, since the race weekend filled hotels across the island in 2026 [2].
Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on a local news report of the 2026 race, reports on the 2024 race, the organiser's announcements, a race listing and the airport weather archive.

faqs.question: How many runners took part in the Bohol International Marathon in 2026?
faqs.answer: More than 5,600 local and international runners, according to Cebu Daily News, which called it a record. The 2024 race had 3,000 participants. The 2026 race was run on Sunday 30 August on Panglao and, by the report's account, filled hotels, restaurants and resorts across the island.

faqs.question: How fast do you need to be to place at the Bohol International Marathon?
faqs.answer: Not as fast as at bigger races. In 2026 third place in the marathon was 2:45:34 for men and 3:39:47 for women, and the winners ran 2:32:40 and 3:21:40. In the half marathon, third woman ran 1:53:18. The 2024 marathon was won in 2:41:31 and 3:55:28.

faqs.question: What is on the Bohol International Marathon course?
faqs.answer: In 2026, mobile DJs, enhanced hydration stations and a new sari-sari store stop with local snacks, according to the race report. Runners were also met by welcome lounges at the airport and seaport, with carbo-loading at the start line. The 2024 race had stations serving lechon baka and lechon baboy.

faqs.question: Who hosts the Bohol International Marathon?
faqs.answer: BE Grand Resort Bohol in Panglao, which gives the race its name. A three-year hosting deal signed in 2024 ran to 2026, and on race day in 2026 the resort and the organisers extended the partnership through 2030. The 2027 race is on Sunday 22 August 2027.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-29 to the template, about the race run on 30 August 2026. Thin material: one post-race report, so the review is short. The Cebu Daily News page returns a bot check to this session's fetches; its text was read from a copy the coordinating session saved from an ordinary browser page load. The report's podium lists are unlabelled; distance labels are inferred from the times, and the review says so. 'World Athletics-accredited' and 'fourth edition' are the report's words; the race itself is older (listings go back to 2012); the resort's hosting deal dates from 2024. No start times, route map, time limits or 2026 fees could be found; 2025 fees are given as last year's. No local airport weather record exists for race morning, so there is no weather section. Official results sit behind a bot check and were not used. No first-hand runner account of 2026 was found. No rating.
